Build an edit op

Source: R/ops.R
ops.Rd

Constructors for the operations build_scenario() applies. Each returns the plain list you would otherwise write by hand, so a constructor-built op, a hand-written one and one parsed from an agent's JSON are interchangeable:

Usage

op_set(value, target = NULL, during = NULL)

op_scale(by, target = NULL, during = NULL)

op_delta(by, target = NULL, during = NULL)

op_delta_each(by, target = NULL, during = NULL)

op_total(value, target = NULL, during = NULL)

op_add(...)

op_drop(target = NULL, during = NULL)

op_shift(days, target = NULL, during = NULL)

op_restage(from, to, target = NULL, during = NULL)

Arguments

value

A single number: planned spend per row (op_set()) or for the matched rows in total (op_total()). Not negative.

target

Optional named list of grain column = value(s) selecting the rows to act on, e.g. list(channel = c("TV", "Radio")). Omit to match every row.

during

Optional list(from =, to =) narrowing to rows in market at any point in that window.

by

A single number: the multiplier (op_scale(), not negative) or the amount to add (op_delta(), op_delta_each(); negative to cut).

...

For op_add(): the new line item's columns, named.

days

A whole number of days; negative moves earlier.

from, to

The new in-market dates: Date, POSIXct, or ISO-8601 strings.

Value

A plain list: one edit op, ready for the edits argument of build_scenario() on its own or in a list of ops.

Details

op_scale(1.2, target = list(channel = "TV"))
# is exactly
list(scale = 1.2, target = list(channel = "TV"))

What a constructor adds is checking where the op is written: a wrong type, a backwards window or an unparseable date errors here, before any plan is involved. Whether the target exists in a particular plan can only be known when the op is applied, so build_scenario() checks that.

Fields come out in a fixed order – the operation, then target, then during – and fields not given are left out, so identical() holds against a hand-written op in that order. build_scenario() does not care about order.

Operations

See Edit forms in build_scenario() for the full rules.

op_set()

Put value on each matched row.

op_total()

Make the matched rows sum to value, holding their mix.

op_scale()

Multiply each matched row by by.

op_delta()

Move the matched rows' sum by by, holding their mix. The usual way to say "take 50k out of TV".

op_delta_each()

Add by to each matched row.

op_transfer()

Move an amount from one set of rows to another, leaving the plan's total unchanged. Documented on its own page.

op_add()

Introduce a line item, named by its columns in ...: every line item column, planned_spend, and either the plan's time column or flight_start and flight_end.

op_drop()

Remove the matched rows entirely.

op_shift()

Move the matched flights by days.

op_restage()

Move the matched flights to run from–to.

op_rebound()

Change the spend bounds on the matched rows, and no spend. Documented on its own page.

See also

build_scenario() to apply ops; plan_ops_schema() for the JSON Schema an agent's ops are checked against.

Examples

op_scale(1.2, target = list(channel = "Search"))
#> $scale
#> [1] 1.2
#> 
#> $target
#> $target$channel
#> [1] "Search"
#> 
#> 

identical(op_scale(1.2, target = list(channel = "Search")),
          list(scale = 1.2, target = list(channel = "Search")))
#> [1] TRUE

op_add(channel = "Audio", week = "2026-07-06", planned_spend = 25)
#> $add
#> $add$channel
#> [1] "Audio"
#> 
#> $add$week
#> [1] "2026-07-06"
#> 
#> $add$planned_spend
#> [1] 25
#> 
#> 
op_restage("2026-08-03", "2026-08-30", target = list(channel = "TV"))
#> $restage
#> $restage$from
#> [1] "2026-08-03"
#> 
#> $restage$to
#> [1] "2026-08-30"
#> 
#> 
#> $target
#> $target$channel
#> [1] "TV"
#> 
#> 

# A malformed op errors where it is written.
try(op_shift(2.5))
#> Error : op_shift(): `shift` must be a single whole number of days (negative to move earlier).

base <- media_plan_from_df(
  data.frame(week = as.Date("2026-07-06"),
             channel = c("TV", "Search", "Social"),
             planned_spend = c(80, 40, 40)),
  grain = "channel", time = "week", name = "base"
)
build_scenario(base, name = "trim TV, drop Social", edits = list(
  op_delta(-10, target = list(channel = "TV")),
  op_drop(target = list(channel = "Social"))
))
#> <MediaPlan> trim TV, drop Social  [in development]
#>   grain       channel + week
#>   flight      2026-07-06 to 2026-07-12  (1 week)
#>   line items  2
#>     channel   Search, TV
#>   rows        2
#>   spend       110
#>   id          plan_f0e365   derived from plan_72dfcc
#> 
#>          week channel planned_spend
#>    2026-07-06      TV            70
#>    2026-07-06  Search            40
